page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the server includes 1843 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities in memory-intensive and data-centric operations. The server achieves a strong rating in large-block memory bandwidth, reaching 260.21 GB/sec for read-only and 127.25 GB/sec for write operations. Passmark database operations and memory scores are also in the top 25% tier, registering at 22,997.62 and 2,844.62 respectively. Static web serving throughput is highly efficient at 48.57 GB/sec. CPU-bound tasks, such as stress-ng multi-core performance and Geekbench multi-core compiling, perform in the average range. However, large-scale LLM text generation is a notable bottleneck, with the 70B model text generation scoring in the bottom 10% at 2.33 tokens/sec due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48ds_v5 offers a balanced profile for enterprise workloads requiring high memory density and local storage without the premium cost of specialized GPU accelerators. The inclusion of 1843 GB of local storage and high-speed memory bandwidth makes it highly suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching, and data warehousing. It is also well-suited for high-throughput web serving and memory-intensive data processing pipelines, while workloads requiring heavy parallel floating-point computations or large language model inference are better served by GPU-accelerated alternatives.
